limitations: Original reauth5 fails at unlink of a nonexistent destination with OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND; later assertions remain unverified.
Windows native first-write failure at e9c7f8b requires reacceptance. Its encrypted size-shaped SET_INFO and self-recall support this correction but do not prove the native test is fixed.
SMB leases, other metadata transitions, namespace handle exclusion, NFS delegation and broader Full SMB/NFS gates remain open.
Windows NFS OPEN INVAL and earlier EXCHANGE_ID timeout root causes remain unresolved; a subsequent passing NFS run does not explain them.
diagnostic_note: A local transparent proxy observed original reauth4 sending SET_INFO and receiving STATUS_PENDING followed by an oplock break, then failing INVALID_NETWORK_RESPONSE. Correcting the inapplicable classic-oplock recall makes the unmodified case pass. The proxy recorded only frame headers and NTLM flags/lengths, no credentials or data. Condensed upstream report omits service snapshots/server log; sha256 identifies the original full report.
